name: Morgan / Helios
notes: Morgan Blake joined from Gmail. Conversation was the Plant 3 rollout at Keystone — steel mill, production supervisors, a forecast for the new line. Not a professional-services or legal motion.

action_items.text: Send a Plant 3 rollout outline: supervisor meeting cadence and what we need from the mill’s CRM
Share the Plant 3 org chart and the current production-forecast spreadsheet

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Morgan, thanks for grabbing time. Calendar just had a Gmail. I want to make sure I know which Morgan I'm talking to.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Happens a lot. I'm Morgan Blake. Personal Gmail because I'm on site at the mill this week and the corporate laptop is being imaged. I'm at Keystone — Keystone Steel. I'm here about the Plant 3 rollout, not anything else you might have under my name.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Plant 3, steel. Tell me what rollout means on your side.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Plant 3 is the new line. We need the supervisors to forecast output and the commercial team to forecast the tons that line will sell. Right now it's a spreadsheet taped to a whiteboard. I want that in a system before we hire the next wave of AEs who will sell Plant 3 capacity.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: So this is an industrial rollout. Floor plus commercial, not a professional-services firm trying to forecast matters.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Correct. We pour steel. I don't sit in a law office. Keystone, Plant 3, mill in Ohio. The work on our side has been living as Keystone Plant 3.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: Got it. For a plant rollout we usually start with the commercial forecast — tons, price, ship month — and keep the supervisor meeting simple. I don't want to boil the mill in week one.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Please don't. The plant manager will walk if we show them a sales dashboard. They need a weekly number they can argue with. The AEs need to see which tons are actually committed versus which are wishful.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: We can split those views. Same underlying records, different meeting. Are you still the commercial owner for Plant 3, or did that move?

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: I'm still the owner. I just couldn't get a Keystone calendar invite out from the mill Wi-Fi, which is why you're looking at Gmail. Please keep the work on Keystone Plant 3. I am not starting a side project from a personal inbox.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: I'll recap to this address and to your Keystone email if I have it. Send the Plant 3 org chart and the production-forecast sheet when you're back on the corporate laptop.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Will do. Timing: we heat the line in October. I'd like a working cadence in September so we're not inventing a forecast the week we pour.

transcript.speaker: Priya Shah
transcript.text: I'll send a Plant 3 outline today. Thanks Morgan — good to put a face to the mill context.

transcript.speaker: Morgan Blake
transcript.text: Thanks Priya. Keystone, Plant 3, steel. Talk soon.
